```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 9, fig.height = 3.5)
library(SIR)
python_ready <- all(vapply(c("numpy", "scipy", "numba"),
                          reticulate::py_module_available, logical(1)))
knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval = python_ready)
```

SIR compares a viability surface with Bliss independence, fitting nonincreasing
single-agent curves and a two-dimensional isotonic surface. The primary statistic
measures standardized positive excess. Its reference is a plug-in bootstrap at
exact Bliss. The companion test evaluates mean excess, while a region scan
localizes candidate synergy. Activity is mean `1 - Y` over observed combinations.

Install Python >= 3.9 with numpy, scipy and numba, and select its executable with
`RETICULATE_PYTHON` before starting R. `sir_python_install_help()` prints commands;
`sir_python_config()` reports the selected interpreter. Python is bundled only as
source for `sirsyn`; the interpreter and dependencies are installed separately.
The example chunks evaluate when those dependencies are available.

## Simulated single plate

Rows and columns must be ordered by increasing dose, with zero first. Viability
is normalized to a control of one. This simulation adds Gaussian measurement
noise and a synergy effect at the higher doses.

```{r simulate}
set.seed(21)
doses <- c(0, 0.1, 0.3, 1, 3)
a <- c(1, 0.95, 0.8, 0.55, 0.3)
b <- c(1, 0.9, 0.7, 0.45, 0.25)
Y <- outer(a, b) + matrix(rnorm(25, sd = 0.04), 5)
Y[1, 1] <- 1
Y[3:5, 3:5] <- Y[3:5, 3:5] - 0.12
noise <- sir_noise_parametric(sd = 0.04)
fit <- sir_fit(Y, doses = list(doses, doses), design = "S", noise = noise, seed = 12)
summary(fit)
```

The default first stage uses 399 reference draws. If either the primary or scan
p-value is at most 0.05, a fresh second stage uses 9,999 draws. `t_std` is the
SIR statistic; `p_tstd` and `p_scan` report the final stage; their stage-one values remain available.

```{r surface}
plot(fit)
```

The excess map is descriptive. Region claims use adjusted scan p-values and are
available in `fit$claims`. All indices in claims, logs and fragility fields are
zero-based positions in the original grid: add one to index the R input.

## Replicates, external curves, and missing wells

For replicated data supply an array with dimensions
`c(replicates, rows, columns)`. Design R measures single agents on every plate
and uses a block-level companion t test. S with replicates is relabeled R.
At least three available replicate values are required for screening.

Design P treats the first row and column as external single-agent curves.
The default `sa_replicates = Inf` keeps them fixed and conditions inference on
the reported curves. Finite `sa_replicates` and `sa_rho` propagate specified
curve error. Plate shifts belong in the noise model and the design-P companion
variance. Assay-specific SD curves or residual banks can be estimated with
`sir_sd_from_replicates()` and `sir_noise_bank()`.

```{r missing}
Ym <- Y
Ym[2, 3] <- NA_real_
missing_fit <- sir_fit(Ym, noise = noise, seed = 12)
missing_fit$log$missing_cells
missing_fit$mean_test
```

Missing combinations are excluded without imputation. A missing single-agent
well removes its dose row or column. On incomplete single-plate S grids, the
companion uses bootstrap mean excess at exact Bliss and reports an unavailable SE;
treat that p-value as exploratory. The data log records these decisions. Fits can be saved with `saveRDS()`.

## A declared screening family

```{r screen}
panel <- data.frame(pair = c("A+B", "C+D", "E+F"),
                    family = c("cell-1", "cell-1", "cell-2"))
panel$Y <- list(Y, outer(a, b), outer(a, b))
hits <- sir_screen(panel, design = "S", noise = noise, seed = 15)
hits[c("pair", "family", "p", "q", "call")]
```

BH adjustment is performed within each family. Inspect `attr(hits, "notes")`
for Monte Carlo resolution limits. Calls need independent experimental
confirmation. Region-scan calibration was evaluated by simulation on complete grids with
parametric noise in designs S and P; it has not been evaluated with residual
banks, missing wells, replicate screening or propagated single-agent
uncertainty. Plate shifts were evaluated in design P, not in design S. Fragility flags describe
sensitivity to influential cells and single-agent doses; they are not outlier tests.
